'''Daniel Milton Neumark''' (born 27 March 1955)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neumark |first=Daniel |author-link=Daniel M. Neumark |date=March 2021 |title=CURRICULUM VITAE; DANIEL M. NEUMARK |url=https://bromine.cchem.berkeley.edu/DMN_CV_March2021.pdf |url-status=live |access-date=21 December 2025}}</ref> is an American chemist and professor of chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

==Education==
Neumark obtained his B.A. and M.A. from [[Harvard University]], working as an undergraduate in the lab of [[Dudley R. Herschbach|Dudley Herschbach]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Neumark |first=Daniel M. |date=2021-12-09 |title=Autobiography of Daniel M. Neumark |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.1c09362 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |volume=125 |issue=48 |pages=10257–10263 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpca.1c09362 |issn=1089-5639|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He went on to earn his [[Ph.D.]] in [[physical chemistry]] from [[University of California, Berkeley]]<ref name=":0" /> in the lab of future Nobel laureate [[Yuan T. Lee]].

==Career and research==
From 1984 to 1986 he was a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral]] fellow at [[University of Colorado]], in the lab of [[William Carl Lineberger|W. Carl Lineberger]] at [[JILA]].<ref name=":0" /> He currently is a professor at [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=":0" /> He was the director of the [[chemical sciences]] division at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] from 2000 to 2010.<ref name=":0" />

Neumark specializes in the use of ultra-high vacuum techniques (including [[molecular beam]]s) and photochemistry to characterize the quantum states of elusive or short-lived chemical entities in the gas phase.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gabrielsen |first1=Paul |date=29 January 2016 |title=QnAs with Daniel Neumark |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=113 |issue=7 |pages=1679–1680 |bibcode=2016PNAS..113.1679G |doi=10.1073/pnas.1600085113 |pmc=4763775 |pmid=26825112 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel Neumark New Director of Chemical Sciences Division |url=https://www2.lbl.gov/Science-Articles/Archive/neumark-csd.html |website=www2.lbl.gov}}</ref> His research has involved the probing [[transition state]]s using negative ion [[photoelectron spectroscopy]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kunin |first=Alice |last2=Li |first2=Wei-Li |last3=Neumark |first3=Daniel M. |date=2018-08-28 |title=Dynamics of electron attachment and photodissociation in iodide-uracil-water clusters via time-resolved photoelectron imaging |url=https://pubs.aip.org/jcp/article/149/8/084301/565791/Dynamics-of-electron-attachment-and |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |language=en |volume=149 |issue=8 |doi=10.1063/1.5040673 |issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription }}</ref> investigation of the properties and dynamics of [[hydrated electron]]s using [[Time-resolved spectroscopy|time-resolved]] photoelectron spectroscopy on [[water cluster]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Asmis |first=Knut R. |last2=Santambrogio |first2=Gabriele |last3=Zhou |first3=Jia |last4=Garand |first4=Etienne |last5=Headrick |first5=Jeffrey |last6=Goebbert |first6=Daniel |last7=Johnson |first7=Mark A. |last8=Neumark |first8=Daniel M. |date=2007-05-21 |title=Vibrational spectroscopy of hydrated electron clusters(H2O)15–50− via infrared multiple photon dissociation |url=https://pubs.aip.org/jcp/article/126/19/191105/929591/Vibrational-spectroscopy-of-hydrated-electron |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |language=en |volume=126 |issue=19 |doi=10.1063/1.2741508 |issn=0021-9606|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0011-00CD-E |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Neumark and fellow Berkeley professor [[Stephen Leone]] have collaborated on research probing [[quantum dynamics]] using [[Attosecond physics|attosecond spectroscopy]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Neumark Group - Research Interests |url=https://sites.google.com/berkeley.edu/dmngrp/research-interests |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=sites.google.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel M. Neumark – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/daniel-m-neumark-jtaktp/ |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=www.nasonline.org/ |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gaynor |first=James D. |last2=Fidler |first2=Ashley P. |last3=Kobayashi |first3=Yuki |last4=Lin |first4=Yen-Cheng |last5=Keenan |first5=Clare L. |last6=Neumark |first6=Daniel M. |last7=Leone |first7=Stephen R. |date=2023-02-28 |title=Nonresonant coherent amplitude transfer in attosecond four-wave-mixing spectroscopy |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.107.023526 |journal=Physical Review A |language=en |volume=107 |issue=2 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.107.023526 |issn=2469-9926|arxiv=2211.12694 }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Neumark won the [[William F. Meggers Award]] in 2005, the [[Irving Langmuir Award]] in 2008, the [[Herbert P. Broida Prize]] in 2013, the [[Bourke Award]] in 2018<ref>{{Cite news |title=Prizes and awards 2018 |url=https://www.rsc.org/news/2018/may/prizes-and-awards-2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710112442/https://www.rsc.org/news/2018/may/prizes-and-awards-2018 |archive-date=2025-07-10 |access-date=2025-12-21 |work=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en-GB}}</ref> and the [[Peter Debye Award]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=College of Chemistry faculty and alums among ACS 2019 National Award winners {{!}} College of Chemistry |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/college-chemistry-faculty-and-alums-among-acs-2019-national-award-winners |access-date=2025-12-21 |website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> He is an Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/neumark-daniel |title=Daniel Neumark |publisher=aaas.org |access-date=May 14, 2017 |archive-date=November 15, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115083437/https://www.aaas.org/fellow/neumark-daniel |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/neumark |title=Daniel Neumark |publisher=berkeley.edu |access-date=May 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bromine.cchem.berkeley.edu/ |title=Lab |publisher=berkeley.edu |access-date=May 14, 2017}}</ref>
